newsitem.title: NORWAY: Statoil hopes for gas sales deal with Italy soon.
newsitem.headline: Statoil hopes for gas sales deal with Italy soon.

text.p: Norway has still not finalised a gas supply agreement with Italy, but hopes the deal will be sealed soon, state-owned Den norske stats oljeselskap AS (Statoil) said on Tuesday.
Italian state gas company SNAM SpA, a subsidiary of ENI SpA, has been in negotiations with Norway's Gas Negotiating Committee (GFU), which comprises Statoil, Norsk Hydro ASA and Saga Petroleum ASA.
Statoil has previously said it hoped to complete negotiations before the end of the year.
"We have been negotiating with SNAM for a long time. We hope to have an agreement soon," Statoil spokeswoman Wenche Skorge told Reuters.
Skorge declined to comment on a report in the daily Stavanger Aftenblad on Monday that Norway and Italy had signed a supply deal to come into effect in 2000.
The daily said deliveries would peak at six billion cubic metres per year in 2006 and continue at that level until 2025.
Under the Troll sales agreements to continental Europe, Norway is in the top five of the global league of gas suppliers along with Algeria, the Netherlands, Indonesia and Russia.

The Scandinavian country, which exports more than three million barrels per day of oil to be the second largest crude exporter after Saudi Arabia, already supplies gas to Germany, the Netherlands, Belgium, France, Austria and Spain.
